svg.title: A dated published critique beside a model window
svg.desc: Keep dated critique and model response as distinct text windows beside the tentative diagram. Neither critic nor model acquires a body, room or privileged narrator position.

Neither critic nor model acquires a body, room or privileged narrator position.", "lettering": [ { "box": [ 0.045, 0.78, 0.91, 0.18 ] } ], "lettering_mode": "manual", "nodes": [ { "asset": "monitor", "box": [ 0.06775, 0.2012, 0.3913, 0.276474 ], "color": "steel", "focus": true, "label": "CRITIQUE 3 SEPTEMBER", "label_box": [ 0.06775, 0.49443, 0.3913, 0.121481 ], "label_size": 18 }, { "asset": "blank-monitor", "box": [ 0.52275, 0.2012, 0.3913, 0.276474 ], "color": "steel", "focus": true, "label": "CHATGPT", "label_box": [ 0.52275, 0.49443, 0.3913, 0.121481 ], "label_size": 18 } ], "reconstructed": false, "shot": "row", "source": "
**Frame:** Recto. Curt's dotted arrow from [page 038](038.md) still points at `INSTRUMENTAL CONVERGENCE`. A second window has opened beside the ChatGPT window: a published critique, in a different typeface, with a byline and a date (`CARL BROWN — INTERNET OF BUGS — 3 SEPTEMBER 2026`). Both are text on screens. Neither has a face.

**Action:** A stranger's argument enters the room by the same door the model uses.

**Caption:**
> ONE OF THESE WINDOWS IS A PERSON.

**Provenance:** `reconstructed` — the scene is invented; the critique is `IOB-CIV`, a real dated publication registered in the source index. The formal point is that the reader cannot tell the two windows apart by looking.
